description:
One guard has three evaluators today (interpreter, body native lowering, receive matcher) with three semantics, none of them the body's: arithmetic is unchecked or host-panics, the matcher's ordering is a signed integer compare, and a helper called from a guard is re-planned and inlined under a syntactic purity whitelist. The planner learns nothing from a guard (Region::Guard is opaque to reachability and keying).

End state: each `when` is a generated function of its subjects and pins returning boolean, compiled by the ordinary body pipeline and activated in guard mode, where a failing callee returns {value, failed}, a `never` call site is failed = true, and the guard answers false on any failed lane (Elixir's rule: a failure in a guard makes the clause not match). Entry dispatch, the receive matcher (through a func ref) and the interpreter all call that function. The three evaluators, the reify job and its fact, and PatternGuardDispatch are deleted.

Purity is one fact per function on the World, `allocates` and `fails`, monotone, derived over the lowered body and static callees, declared on `extern "fz"`. The rule is "allocates nothing that outlives the decision": a static-shape intermediate rides in lanes and a guard returns a boolean so nothing escapes; anything of unbounded size (list construction, binary concatenation, map update) is refused. That is the BEAM's guard-BIF line, reached by construction. Binary patterns decide with a three-word cursor and bind three-word views that materialize on the consumer's heap at clause entry, which is also what lets the receive matcher run on the sender's side without touching a heap.

Order: fz-5xp.20 (no arithmetic_result tuple) and the bitstring reader in lanes, then the effects fact, then guards as code (after fz-21x.10 gives the matcher a caller), then the enforced matcher contract. Proof fixtures: guard_arithmetic_failure (Elixir oracle), guard_overflow, the receive float guard, the ===-in-guard cases, the wildcard-named helper parameter, and heap-counter pins of zero allocation on the probing side.

Stacked on PR #158 (fz-5xp.30). Grew out of fz-21x step 8, which was never part of the .30 contract.

title: [EPIC] Guards are code: one guard function per clause, failure is false, the matcher calls it
